summary: Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education around 1962–1966. He held positions at Doshisha University and Kyoto University, serving as professor at Kyoto around 1992–2006.

Tsuruji Sahoda was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Kyoto University from around 1923 to 1926. He held academic posts at Osaka University (circa 1949–1962) and Ritsumeikan University (circa 1962–1970).
Tsutomu Hatai was an Indology scholar who served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society, where he was attested in 1987 as successor to Hiroshi Maruyama.
Tsutomu Horio is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keiji Nishitani. He held a professorship at Otani University, attested in 1990.

Tsutomu Kubo worked in philosophy, studying under Raphael von Koeber at the University of Tokyo and later earning a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tohoku University (1929; 1940–1946), and Toyo University (~1950–1954).

Tsutomu Yamaguchi works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Hokkaido University. He has served as a collaborative researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a special appointed researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies in 2017.
Tsyben Zhamtsarano was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902. He later headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard Universities, he held faculty posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard (1981–2010), and Peking University, and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008).

Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. His students included Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Tubten Nyendrak studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.
Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Halle until 1912. He held an attested post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, and his teachers included Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery and under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology and founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery. He studied under teachers including Samten Gyatso, and taught numerous students, including the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tuomo Pekkanen is a scholar in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied under Pentti Aalto around 1956–1968 and held a post at the University of Jyväskylä from around 1972 to 2000.
